reason: This passage (1 Kings 17-18) demonstrates Yahweh's protective care and concern for the Hebrew people. Yahweh: (1) provides for Elijah, His servant, during the famine; (2) miraculously sustains a widow and her son with endless flour and oil; (3) restores the widow's son to life; (4) performs a dramatic display of power on Mount Carmel to vindicate Himself before Israel; (5) sends rain to end the famine. While Yahweh is antagonistic toward idolatry and disobedience to His commandments (particularly Ahab's Baal worship), His actions are corrective and restorative toward the Hebrew people themselves. The text portrays Yahweh as actively working to bring the people back to proper worship, not as their adversary.
